content.text:
Finding submitted: **compliant** (sitting at the playbook fallback), no redline proposed.

Key points:
- **Customer assignment protected:** Section 14.1 lets either party — including Corio — assign without consent on a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all related assets. The walk-away scenario (blanket prohibition with no M&A carve-out) does not apply.
- **No change-of-control exit for the Vendor:** Section 11.2 limits termination to uncured material breach and insolvency; document-wide searches for "change of control" and deemed-assignment language returned nothing, so Commerce One gains no termination or re-pricing right on a Corio change of control.
- **Noted, not flagged:** no express affiliate carve-out, and the residual consent right is not qualified as "not to be unreasonably withheld." These are sub-elements short of the preferred wording. The direct-competitor consent proviso is mutual and equally shields Corio, so it is left alone.
